Whether fashion designs are protected under copyright law depends on the jurisdiction and the specific design element in question. [d4] In the United States, clothing designs are generally not protected under copyright law unless they contain a functional or utilitarian aspect, and the law currently favors utility over aesthetics in this space [d4][d2]. However, certain design elements such as graphic designs, textile patterns, and logos can qualify for copyright protection if they demonstrate a sufficient amount of creativity [d1], and the U.S. [d4] Copyright Office has also recognized that two-dimensional designs on the surface of clothing, including combinations of shapes, colors, and arrangements, can be protected by copyright [d1]. Outside the U.S., protection varies greatly from country to country — for example, in the European Union, the Creative Designs Directive and European Designs Directive protect new designs for up to three or five years [d2], while in the U.S., the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) of 1998 brought further limits on fashion design copyrighting [d2].
[[END-OF-ANSWER]]
